process: SAGD thermal in-situ recovery, Canadian oil sands (text)
value: Steam-assisted gravity drainage: two horizontal wells; steam injected in the upper well heats the bitumen, which drains to and is produced from the lower well. Needs thick, clean deposits; uses less energy and recovers more bitumen (about 70%) than cyclic steam stimulation. Steam raised mostly from natural gas in Canada

process: SAGD thermal in-situ recovery, Canadian oil sands (text)
note: p.3: in 2008 Canada had 6 large SAGD facilities producing about 130 kb/d [8]; the brief calls it 'the new, promising' technique.

process: Cyclic steam stimulation (CSS) thermal in-situ recovery, Canadian oil sands (text)
value: Cyclic steam stimulation: steam is injected into vertical wells to heat the bitumen, which is then pumped to the surface through the same well; recovery about 25-30% of the bitumen. TRAP: the brief writes 'CCS' for cyclic steam stimulation (CSS) throughout the oil-sand text ('two large CCS facilities', 'SOR ... 3.4 for CCS', 'about 70% against 25%-30% from CCS') and misnames it 'Cycle Steam Simulator' - it is NOT carbon capture and storage.

process: Oil sand surface mining with hot-water extraction (text)
value: Surface mining of oil sand within about 75 m of the surface: oil sand is shovelled by large machines and hauled to an extraction plant, where bitumen is separated from the sand with hot water and chemicals; about 90% of the bitumen is recovered. The bitumen is sold raw or upgraded to synthetic crude oil

value: Upgrading of bitumen to a lighter synthetic crude oil by raising the hydrogen-to-carbon ratio, either by removing carbon (coking) or adding hydrogen (hydrocracking)
